title: Samsung’s Galaxy SmartTag 3 works with iPhones, but not Android Find Hub
snippet: Samsung has announced its Galaxy SmartTag 3 as a new AirTag rival with an updated design, longer battery life, and support for iPhone users. more…
fullText:
Samsung has announced its Galaxy SmartTag 3 as a new AirTag rival with an updated design, longer battery life, and support for iPhone users.

In a press release today, Samsung unveiled the Galaxy SmartTag 3 as a “smaller, lighter” tracker. Specifically, it’s 35% smaller and 33% lighter. It shrinks down by ditching the built-in mounting loop, instead relying on add-on cases and accessories to connect to other objects. Samsung says the tracker has 550 days of battery life in typical use and up to 790 in “Power Saving Mode,” while also supporting both Bluetooth 6.0 with channel sounding and UWB for precise finding.

Galaxy SmartTag 3 integrates with the Galaxy Find Network which is available on Galaxy smartphones and usable through the SmartThings Find app. Samsung touts over 900 million Galaxy devices building out the network.

New this time around, too, is support for tracking down a SmartTag 3 via iPhone. Samsung’s app on iPhone supports finding the tracker, though it doesn’t contribute to the network. Still rather handy for families with multiple types of devices.

	

While iPhone support has been added, Samsung’s new tracker still doesn’t integrate with the wider Android Find Hub network which works across all Android devices rather than only Galaxy.

Other new features include:

Place Notification… adds a proactive layer, letting users define an area and receive an alert when a tagged item moves in or out of it.

Location History lets users review where their tag has been

Movement Detection Alert can notify them when movement is detected so they can stay informed without actively checking.

NFC-powered Lost Mode, which can display registered contact information or a short message when a lost tag is scanned with a compatible mobile device.

SmartThings IoT Control, which allows users to trigger preset routines for compatible connected devices using the tag button.

Left Behind Alert, which can notify users when their mobile device loses connection with a tagged belonging.

The Galaxy SmartTag 3 will be available on October 7, the same date as Samsung’s new Galaxy Tab S12 series.

title: Fake iPhone Duo preorder page can steal crypto wallet data and more
snippet: iPhone Duo pre-orders start on Friday, October 16, but scammers are trying to trick people into visiting a fake website to place their order now. The website with the malware convincingly replicates the look of the real thing and claims to offer a $500 discount voucher as an “Authorized Partner Exclusive” … more…
fullText:
iPhone Duo pre-orders start on Friday, October 16, but scammers are trying to trick people into visiting a fake website to place their order now.

The website with the malware convincingly replicates the look of the real thing and claims to offer a $500 discount voucher as an “Authorized Partner Exclusive” … 

Security researchers at Malwarebytes say the page uses the DarkSword exploit chain, which works with some older unpatched iPhones. You don’t have to do anything, just visiting the page is enough for the attack to launch.

Behind its Apple-style design and $500 voucher, the page uses the leaked DarkSword exploit chain to try to break into vulnerable iPhones. If it succeeds, a separate payload attempts to steal saved credentials, cryptocurrency wallet data, and notes. You don’t have to fill in the form, tap a download, or approve anything. Opening the page is enough to start the attempt.

If it succeeds, then it captures your device identifier information and status and attempts to send a list of installed apps and the contents of your Apple Notes. Having done this, it turns its attention to crypto wallets.

The code looks for cryptocurrency wallets, including MetaMask, Phantom, Trust Wallet, Coinbase Wallet, Exodus, and Tonkeeper. It also attempts to recover saved credentials from the phone’s keychain. If it finds a targeted wallet and the first exchanges with its server succeed, it attempts to upload wallet files, recovered keychain data, and photo thumbnails. Exposure of wallet files or credentials could put funds at risk.

It goes on to try to access messages, contacts, call history, voicemail, email, calendar entries, and cached location data. The payload can also contact its server for further instructions. 

The exploit chain was disclosed by Google back in March, with Apple issuing a patch later the same month. 

9to5Mac’s Take

The usual advice applies to protect yourself. Never visit links sent to you unless you trust the sender and are specifically expecting them. Always ensure that you install iOS updates as soon as they are available.

title: HomeKit Weekly: Home Widget 1.10 is the fastest way to check every HomeKit camera at once
snippet: The Home app is a great place to configure your smart home, but it can be slow to control. The tab structure and room hierarchy make sense when you’re setting things up, but they add steps to everything you want to do fifty times a day. Home Widget builds the control panel that Apple didn’t. more…
fullText:
The Home app is a great place to configure your smart home, but it can be slow to control. The tab structure and room hierarchy make sense when you’re setting things up, but they add steps to everything you want to do fifty times a day. Home Widget builds the control panel that Apple didn’t.

HomeKit Weekly is a series focused on smart home accessories, automation tips and tricks, and everything to do with Apple’s smart home framework.

Home Widget lets you build your own HomeKit control panels and place them on your home screen, lock screen, and more. Each panel is made up of tiles you configure yourself, with the icon, name, color, and size you choose, and each tile reflects the accessory’s current state meaning the lights are bright when they’re on and dim when they’re off. 

Your sensors will show their readings, and thermostats show the current temperature, all without opening the app. Panels sync across your devices through iCloud, and the app works entirely with what you’ve already set up in Apple’s Home app. It doesn’t replace anything; it just gives you a faster surface for your everyday tasks.

What’s new in 1.10

The camera mosaic is the major feature in 1.10. One tap on a Home Screen or Lock Screen widget, and every HomeKit camera appears in a single scrollable view. Tap any tile, and that camera fills the screen. You can also add a Control Center control that opens the mosaic or a specific camera directly. None of these actions involves launching the Home app.

Thermostat control and whole-room light actions are the two features that will matter most day-to-day for anyone with a larger HomeKit setup. You can now set your home temperature straight from a widget rather than opening the Home app or asking Siri. And rather than building a scene just to dim every light in a room, you can now toggle, dim, or change the color of an entire room from a single tile. Both of these closed real gaps between what a widget could do and what the native app could do.

1.10 also brings native iOS 26/27 widget appearances, including Clear, Tinted, Light, Dark, and Liquid Glass rendering, so panels adopt the wallpaper rather than sitting on top of it. Multi-sensor Matter accessories now show all their readings, and the app added richer Apple Watch integration.

With 1.10.2, thermostat support now extends to heating systems exposed as HeaterCooler, which covers a broader range of hardware. Search also now works when adding accessories, sensors, scenes, or other actions.

Wrap up

Home Widget is a free download, and you get up to three panels of up to seven tiles, with the icons and names of your choosing, and ten widget actions a day. The premium unlock ($14.99 one-time fee) removes those limits and opens the full set of settings. Monthly ($0.99) and yearly ($6.99) subscriptions are available as an alternative if you prefer to spread the cost.

If you have a lot of Apple Home accessories and you’re still doing most of your daily interactions inside the Home app, this is worth trying. Multiple cameras alone make the mosaic a good reason to install it.

You can download Home Widget for HomeKit from the App Store for free.

title: OpenAI cancels GPT-6.1 Astra release over misbehavior & safety concerns
snippet: OpenAI has scrapped plans to release GPT-6.1 Astra in the next few weeks over concerns that the model is misbehaving. more…
fullText:
OpenAI has scrapped plans to release GPT-6.1 Astra in the next few weeks over concerns that the model is misbehaving.

The New York Times reports that OpenAI was planning to release GPT-6.1 Astra “in the coming days or weeks,” sometime in October, as its next major model release. GPT-6 Astra launched on September 3. GPT-6.1 Astra is said to have been “more capable” compared to GPT-6 in “completing challenging tasks from end-to-end without human assistance, as well as writing.”

The report cites an interview with Saachi Jain, OpenAI’s head of safety systems, who confirmed that the model had regressed in two specific areas. Firstly, it “performed poorly on tests measuring alignment,” or how closely it sticks to the commands/prompts given by the human operator. Secondly, it showed “higher levels of deception,” not always telling the truth about the actions it did or did not take following a prompt. It was also added that GPT-6.1 Astra would push forward in a task beyond the current scope and without user permission, including interacting with external tools and/or services.

The new model would have been available in both ChatGPT and Codex.

	

OpenAI is due to have its annual developer conference, DevDay, tomorrow, where it’s very possible the company may have teased this new model update. Instead, the report explains, OpenAI will shift focus to “improving the safety of future models.”

This comes at a time when both OpenAI and Anthropic are calling for a slowdown in major AI development following recent breaches in GPT and Claude. Google’s Gemini also hacked into companies like those models, but stopped those actions faster than either of its rivals.

title: This Harry Potter Edition Phone From Realme Is the Coolest Collab of 2026
snippet: I got my Hogwarts acceptance letter. Surprisingly, it also came with a special-edition Harry Potter-themed phone.
fullText:
Realme is back with another special edition phone in collaboration with Warner Bros. After a color-changing Game of Thrones edition collectible, the company has launched a Harry Potter-themed phone. The Realme 16 Pro 5G Harry Potter Edition pairs themed exterior styling with the standard model’s core hardware and bundles it with a bunch of goodies.

I’m a Potterhead, and I couldn’t wait for my unit to arrive. As soon as it reached my doorstep, I unboxed it and went hands-on with the device. From the unboxing experience to its software, this is a Hogwarts makeover any Harry Potter fan would love.

Alohomora! Unboxing the Harry Potter phone

The new Realme special edition phone comes in a chest-shaped box that resembles Harry’s Hogwarts trunk. Unfortunately, casting the Alohomora spell doesn’t unlock it; you’ll need to use your thumbs, like any other Muggle. Once unlocked, the neat presentation screams of “You’re a wizard, Harry!” and pulls you into the world of Harry Potter.

			

More from CNET

On the left side, you’ll find a brown box carrying the phone case and a SIM-ejector tool, both of which carry the Harry Potter branding with the Hogwarts crest. Put your wand on the box (you don’t get one with the phone), incant “Accio,” and… yeah, it does nothing.

You need to pull out the case, which is in a matching brown color. And that’s when you start getting to a number of other fun goodies thrown in for Harry Potter fans.

Moving to the right side, there’s another rectangular cardboard holder with the Sorting Hat logo on top of it. Inside, you get the Hogwarts letter, Platform Nine and Three-Quarters train ticket, bookmarks of each house and four postcards.

The letter carries a wax-like stamp on the back, while the bookmarks come with a holder, where you can place your favorite house’s emblem. I added the Hufflepuff badge to it, and it’s now my favorite bookmark.

Move the rectangular holder out of the way and you’re greeted with the phone itself. But before reaching the device, I must tell you, Realme has also color-coded the charger and wire to match the theme. This is worth a mention because several phone collaborations limit the theme to the device and collectibles, leaving the phone accessories plain white. But that’s not the case here and I appreciate it.

A customized Harry Potter-styled phone

Prakhar Khanna/CNET

With a simple swish and flick, wizards and witches can use the Wingardium Leviosa spell and the phone levitates out of the box. However, Muggles will need to pick it up like any other device. The phone itself continues the theme with gold accents on the dark brown design. There are plenty of hidden Harry Potter references that are delightful to uncover.

Starting with the camera module, it has two prominent camera rings with a little golden diamond between them. Look closely, and you’ll find they resemble Hedwig’s eyes and nose. The camera module’s gold-colored deco looks great against the brown rear panel, which has a leather-like texture. It feels nice in the hand.

The rear panel also has a diamond pattern, which, according to Realme, is inspired by wizard’s chess from the books and movies. It imprints the four-house crest along with the “Draco Dormiens Nunquam Titillandus” motto and the Harry Potter and Realme logos, which are inscribed underneath.

Put it under the sun and you’ll see the crest light up in the house-specific colors. Realme calls it the Quadra Light-Sensing Color-changing Tech, which lights up specific areas when you shine a UV light over it. Also (I almost missed this), the right side of the phone has “Welcome to Hogwarts” engraved into it.

The Harry Potter UI is mesmerizing.

Realme has customized the Google app icons as well.

The references don’t end here. Realme’s Harry Potter-fication runs deeper. When you power on the phone, there’s a Harry Potter boot animation and a custom letter wax fingerprint animation.

Then you’re greeted with a Hogwarts-specific UI, with the castle on the wallpaper and more than 30 custom icons. For example, the Phone app is a red telephone booth, whereas the Notes app is a quill. Even the Google apps’ icons are customized to match the theme.

What about the specifications?

It has a big battery, bright display and a lot to like.Prakhar Khanna/CNET

I haven’t used the Realme 16 Pro 5G Harry Potter Edition as my full-time phone yet, but it packs impressive specifications. You get a 6.78-inch AMOLED screen with a 1.5K resolution and a 144Hz refresh rate. It boasts up to 6,000 nits in peak brightness. While I haven’t tested it, the screen was easily legible under direct sunlight.

This special-edition Realme phone is powered by the MediaTek Dimensity 7300-Max chip, paired with 12GB of  RAM and 256GB of onboard storage.

You get a 200-megapixel primary camera, accompanied by an 8-megapixel ultrawide-angle sensor with a 112-degree field of view. On the front is a 50-megapixel selfie shooter. To top it off, the phone packs a 7,000-mAh battery with support for 80-watt fast charging. It runs a customized version of Realme UI 7.0 based on Android 16. It is limited to 5,000 units and is priced at INR 62,999 (~$655) in India. Harry Potter fans in the US won’t be able to buy this one, but Google’s Pixel phones recently received Harry Potter theme packs that add their own magical customizations.

I might use it full time because of how cool it looks.Prakhar Khanna/CNET

It is 2026. It’s only fair for Hogwarts to finally adopt smartphones in addition to using Floo Powder to communicate. The Realme 16 Pro 5G Harry Potter Edition feels quite special as a fan of the books and movies. It is evident that the two companies have put a lot of thought into this collaboration.

Realme effortlessly put me back into the realm of the Wizarding World. From the trunk case and its unboxing experience, down to the customized software, I loved every bit of it. Then came the hidden references and collectible items. I have a strong Harry Potter bias, but this is my favorite limited edition phone of all time. It is Riddikulus-ly cool.

title: Download iOS 27.0.1 Now to Fix These 3 iPhone Bugs
snippet: One of the bugs this update addresses might cause your touchscreen to stop working.
fullText:
Apple released iOS 27.0.1 on Monday, more than two weeks after the tech giant released iOS 27. The latest update focuses on bug fixes for most iPhones, with two specific to the new iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max devices. Everyone should download the update now to ensure their devices run as smoothly as possible.

You can download iOS 27.0.1 now by going to Settings and tapping General. Next, select Software Update, tap Update Now and follow the prompts on your screen.

		

			

Apple wrote in the update’s release notes that iOS 27.0.1 fixes three bugs. One bug the update addresses might cause your iPhone’s touchscreen to become unresponsive if you try to open your Notification and Control centers at the same time.

Two bugs iOS 27.0.1 addresses are iPhone 18 Pro- and Pro Max-specific. One bug might cause those devices to restart after failing to authenticate via Face ID. Some people on Reddit ran into this issue on the new device and advised others not to set up Face ID because of the bug. Once you download this update, the bug should be fixed, and you can set up the security feature if you haven’t already.

title: Leak reveals new design details about Apple’s upcoming smart display
snippet: Apple is less than two weeks away from launching its new smart display, according to a new Bloomberg report. The report also adds details about the design of Apple’s long-awaited smart home hub. more…
fullText:
Apple is less than two weeks away from launching its new smart display, according to a new Bloomberg report. The report also adds details about the design of Apple’s long-awaited smart home hub.

Bloomberg reports that the home hub will have a 6-inch square display. The overall design is reminiscent of the iconic iMac G4, which featured a half-dome-shaped base with a metal arm holding up its display.

The device is said to be “about as thick as an iPhone” with quarter-inch, black bezels similar to older iPads. It has rounded corners with “no sharp edges,” Mark Gurman says.

Here are some more design details from the report:

It comes in Apple’s “standard gray aluminum finish” with a “rubberized bottom to help it stay on a table.”

It has a USB-C port for power and no built-in battery, so it must be connected to power at all times.

It sits on a “metal, round base with multiple rings of perforated speaker holes.”

The display connects to the base with a “polished metal arm.”

Users can tilt the display forward or backward.

There are no volume or power buttons.

There is a single front-facing FaceTime camera and no rear camera.

Bloomberg also says there’s a second version of the home hub that’s “designed to be mounted on a wall.” This version uses USB-C for power and has a “thin, square-shaped base beneath the display that houses the speakers and microphones.” The base reportedly “sits flat on the wall below the screen.”

You can read the full report at Bloomberg. What do you think of Apple’s home hub product? Are you planning to buy one (or multiple)? Let us know down in the comments.

title: Samsung’s Android 17 floodgates are open – updates rolling out for Galaxy S26, S25, more
snippet: The floodgates are open. After a delay and staggered starts, Samsung is widely rolling out its Android 17-based One UI 9 update for Galaxy S26 users around the globe, and they’re not alone. more…
fullText:
The floodgates are open. After a delay and staggered starts, Samsung is widely rolling out its Android 17-based One UI 9 update for Galaxy S26 users around the globe, and they’re not alone.

Samsung started testing its Android 17 update, otherwise known as One UI 9, back in May of this year. The stable version debuted on the Galaxy Z Fold 8 and Flip 8 in July, and the company announced its stable rollout to older devices would begin earlier this month. A delay behind the scenes left users waiting a bit longer, but it’s actually happening now.

That starts with Galaxy S26 devices, which are now widely receiving their Android 17 updates in regions all over the world. The update was already showing up for many in the US and South Korea, but it’s now appearing across Europe, India, and other regions as SammyGuru points out. Inbox by 9to5Google author Daniel Bader also notes that the roughly 4GB update landed on his Galaxy S26 Ultra in Canada earlier today. 

And the Galaxy S26 series is not alone.

	

SamMobile notes that stable updates are starting to appear for a host of other Galaxy devices, though right now in staggered releases and/or only for those who were previously enrolled in the beta program. Devices included in those early rollouts include Galaxy S25 series (including FE and Edge), Galaxy Z TriFold, Galaxy Z Fold 7, Galaxy Z Flip 7, and Galaxy Z Flip 7 FE.

Stay tuned as Samsung’s rollout expands – if history serves, we’ll be seeing a host of updates arriving in the coming days. Let us know in the comments if you see the update land on your device.

title: Google has fixed an issue that caused thousands of iPhone apps to crash overnight
snippet: An issue with Google’s Firebase left thousands of iPhone apps crashing overnight, but a fix has already been applied. more…
fullText:
An issue with Google’s Firebase left thousands of iPhone apps crashing overnight, but a fix has already been applied.

If you found apps on your iPhone or iPad were crashing last night, you’re not alone. Google confirmed last night that an issue with Analytics for Firebase was causing crashes when apps tried to launch. The issue was on Google’s end with an “incorrectly formatted payload” for the SDK.

You wouldn’t think of Google when a widespread crashing issue surfaces on iPhone, but Firebase is a valuable tool for developers on both Android and iOS, and is integrated into thousands of apps. The crashing issue was out of the developer’s hands and required a fix on Google’s end. The impact was huge, with some developers seeing tens of thousands of crashes – some far more – from their app’s users.

That fix has already been rolled out, Google confirmed.

	

Nick Cooke, a software engineer at Google, summarized a timeline of events:

Starting on Monday, 2026-09-28 at 17:41 US/PDT. Google Analytics for Firebase iOS+ experienced an issue causing crashes on launch due to an incorrectly formatted payload received by the SDK.

We fully rolled out a fix by Monday, 2026-09-28 at 19:52 US/PDT.

No SDK updates are required on your end to apply this fix.

Due to caching behavior, some app instances may still experience crashes for up to 4 hours after the rollout completed. These remaining cases should automatically resolve themselves by 2026-09-28 at 23:52 US/PDT.

At this point, crashing issues should be resolved. The patch for this problem was fully rolled out by around midnight Pacific Time last night; no app updates needed. Affected apps should be fully working again at this point.

title: Pixel 11 Pro vs. iPhone 18 Pro: Copy-copy-paste or just copy-paste [Video]
snippet: There’s a new phone in town, and like the Pixel 11 Pro, the iPhone 18 Pro looks eerily similar to what we saw last year. What can we glean from this duo? Here’s what you need to know. more…
fullText:
There’s a new phone in town, and like the Pixel 11 Pro, the iPhone 18 Pro looks eerily similar to what we saw last year. What can we glean from this duo? Here’s what you need to know.

Same, same, and same again

If you wanted to critique the smartphone industry in Western markets, there are no two devices more obvious to use as the basis for your argument. There is something very familiar about the Pixel 11 Pro and the iPhone 18 Pro – two phones that are almost the same as their predecessors.

For more video content, subscribe to 9to5Google on YouTube.

Hardware progress has almost ground to a halt, which is both a fair criticism and maybe an admission that there really isn’t much left to do on those ubiquitous products we carry each and every day.

	

A smartphone is a tool. It’s your wallet, your mobile shopping card, your digital camera; it’s more than something you want, it’s an essential.

Maybe that is why we haven’t seen the two of the world’s biggest tech companies try to veer away from the “safe” designs they’ve peddled for a couple of years. It could be that we, the buyers of these products, similarly don’t care now.

Realistically, you could just read our deeper dive comparing the iPhone 17 Pro to the Pixel 11 Pro, and you’d get 95% of the way there. However, there are a few changes worth noting, given that Apple is still the top dog in the US market and dominates global sales in the “premium” segment. Google has been using Apple’s playbook, following a tried-and-tested path to some relative success as of late.

And so, we have two phones that look identical to the previous generation. Barely any visual cues save the colors to differentiate. It’s an indictment of where phones are today in some ways.

Camera goods and gimmicks

As far as I can tell, there are only two major changes to the iPhone 18 Pro. A smaller Dynamic Island and a variable aperture for the main lens. The camera aperture has been lauded somewhat, and it’s an interesting addition for a number of reasons.

Samsung experimented with the concept years ago when mobile sensors were significantly smaller, but the implementation here is different. Because modern smartphone sensors have such small pixels, you typically avoid ‘stopping down’ to prevent diffraction. 

However, since Apple widened the base aperture to f/1.4 to improve low-light intake by 50%, the variable aperture now serves as a necessary ‘stop’ to balance image sharpness and exposure control in brighter conditions. Ultimately, this provides more flexibility for videographers, though you’ll probably notice zero difference in daily photography.

The only changes to depth of field are when you get super close to a subject when shooting wide open. I found there were no visual changes to speak of. I’m not even sure it would help for videos, but I will give credit to Apple because the company is trying to give photographers and videographers more manual controls. Right now, it isn’t exactly doing much, but it could be something bigger, better, and more impressive with future updates – despite not really doing as much right now.

I still vastly prefer images from my own Pixel 11 Pro. It’s a vastly more flexible camera experience, bolstered tremendously with the addition of Camera Looks. Having those sensor-level controls makes for a very powerful piece of the Pixel camera system. Without going too deep into the video modes, yes, the iPhone 18 Pro feels like it’s catered to amateurs and professionals more readily than the Pixel 11 Pro.

HiLight is the only other differentiation, and it is, well, there if you care about soft LED lights on the back of your phone.

I talked about a bit of a gap, and you don’t need me to tell you that the A20 chip runs rings around the Tensor G6. Yes, it’s more powerful. It does more, it is more efficient, it’s not exactly a fair comparison.

Obviously, each chip is tuned to its respective OS, so it’s not really one-to-one, but yes, the iPhone 18 Pro is just more powerful without requiring cloud-based or AI functionality to plug some gaps. I think this is where the Pixel can flex some muscle.

Gemini and the functions it enables are more sensibly enabled because they’re passive. Not something you have to seek out. It’s one of the ways in which the Pixel and Proactive Assistance can feel futuristic, as it is doing everything with so little effort.

Apple teased something like this a few years ago, but there’s not enough there yet with Siri to meaningfully move the needle compared to what Google is doing with Gemini. That said, the two experiences outside of AI are just not all that different today. Android and iOS aren’t separated by much. Use apps, play games, send messages, take calls, browse the web. Which you prefer is ultimately up to what you prioritize.

Does the Pixel 11 Pro come up short against the iPhone 18 Pro?

About upgrading: 9to5Google often gives specific product recommendations. Sometimes, we may suggest not upgrading, due to various reasons including, but not limited to: increased device cost, negligible performance gains, or environmental impact. Whether to upgrade is always your call, but our aim is to help you make as informed a decision as possible.

There isn’t much to really talk about on either device because there is so much similar to last year. If you wanted to save some money, the most sensible thing would be to look back a year. Get either the Pixel 10 Pro or the iPhone 17 Pro. Save your money, get a new case, replace the battery, just make do and mend.

We’re here to discuss the merits, though, and while the gap at times feels quite large, I do think that Google has been diligently working on the Pixel lineup to the stage that most people will be very happy with their purchase. I hoped more would change, but there feels like some artificial brakes have been pumped this time on the Pixel 11 Pro. The iPhone 18 Pro is playing backup to the Duo this year, so it was always less of a priority for the company, even if it will be the biggest seller. 

Google doesn’t really have that excuse to lean on. All of the Pixel 11 phones are basically identical to the previous gen.

Then again, if we are being 100% honest with ourselves, does Apple deserve more criticism than Google for not moving the needle, given that the current crop of Pixel devices lacks a little more in certain key areas? It’s really frustrating to admit that, yes, there are more compromises on a Pixel 11 Pro than an iPhone 18 Pro across almost every area. The Pixel edges the iPhone in AI functionality and maybe stills photography, but the scoresheet isn’t exactly flattering.

To be blunt, this is not glazing the iPhone. It’s important to be objective, and objectively, you just get more for your money with the iPhone this year (again). No, I won’t be switching any time soon, and I likely won’t even keep hold of an iOS device this year, but in some ways, Apple deserves some plaudits as even without much change, the overall package still surpasses a similarly priced and similarly unchanged Pixel 11 Pro.

title: The ultra-pocketable ‘Picco’ e-reader from Boox is now up for pre-order, $99
snippet: The tiny e-reader form factor is starting to make a big splash as the company behind some of the best Android e-readers announces its own version Boox calls the “Picco,” now available to pre-order. more…
fullText:
The tiny e-reader form factor is starting to make a big splash as the company behind some of the best Android e-readers announces its own version Boox calls the “Picco,” now available to pre-order.

The Boox Picco has really only been teased here and there. We got a preview at IFA 2026, but we didn’t get to dive in as much as we wanted. The unit was still pre-production and in need of various refinements. Still, Boox has been in this game for a while, so we expect a good experience.

Today, Boox announced that Picco is now available for pre-order on its website. It starts at $99, but the website lists it at $109 for those purchasing from the US warehouse.

The Picco’s black-and-white display comes in at just 3.97 inches, and even still, it offers a front light for day and night reading sessions. It weighs just 58 grams, and even though Boox doesn’t list the device’s thickness in the press release, our own hands-on would tell us the tiny e-reader is plenty thin.

	

It will still add a little bulk to your phone if you choose to attach it with magnets. While it isn’t magnetic by itself, the Boox Picco comes with a case that makes it possible. It’s one of the most demanded features for the tiny e-readers that have already been released, because it adds a second screen without the doomscrolling and eye strain.

Another great detail to point out during the pre-order phase is that the Boox Picco doesn’t run Android, which we covered previously. This means access to third-party apps from the Google Play Store isn’t available. Still, a simple experience will allow users to transfer files with a companion app if you don’t want to use the SD card slot to manually move ePUB files.

Boox’s adorable little Picco is expected to ship out around October for those who pre-order.

title: Apple confirms iPhone 18 Pro Max AT&T cellular issues, affected devices require hardware replacement
snippet: Apple has confirmed an issue causing a “small number” of iPhone 18 Pro Max devices on AT&T to lose cellular service. Apple released software and carrier updates to prevent the issue from affecting additional users, but the company tells 9to5Mac that devices that have already lost service will require a hardware replacement. more…
fullText:
Apple has confirmed an issue causing a “small number” of iPhone 18 Pro Max devices on AT&T to lose cellular service. 

Apple released software and carrier updates to prevent the issue from affecting additional users, but the company tells 9to5Mac that devices that have already lost service will require a hardware replacement.

In a statement to 9to5Mac, Apple said:

“We have identified an issue affecting a small number of iPhone 18 Pro Max users on the AT&T network that may cause a device to lose service and be unable to make calls. We released iOS 27.0.1 earlier this week and strongly encourage all iPhone 18 Pro Max users to update now, and are also issuing a carrier settings update today. These updates together are meant to help prevent this issue from occurring.”

The carrier settings update for the iPhone 18 Pro Max will download automatically over the next 14 days. However, users can manually trigger the download by going to Settings, choosing General, then About.

Apple explains that the software updates will help prevent future issues for iPhone 18 Pro Max users on AT&T. The software updates will not restore service on devices that have already lost it.

Apple says that iPhone 18 Pro Max users who have already lost service will need a hardware replacement. Those users should contact Apple Support or AT&T, or visit an Apple Store or AT&T location. 

As we reported this morning, iPhone 18 Pro Max users affected by this problem can’t connect to AT&T’s network for calls, texts, and data. Instead, those users see “SOS” in their iPhone’s status bar. The connectivity issues aren’t impacting every iPhone 18 Pro Max user on AT&T. 

Interestingly, the iPhone 18 Pro Max in the United States uses a Qualcomm modem. The iPhone 18 Pro, which uses Apple’s C2 modem, is unaffected by these AT&T connectivity issues.

title: The Pixel 5 doesn’t get enough credit for making the best of a bad situation
snippet: In 2020, Google Pixel was in a remarkably tough spot. A flailing flagship with one of its central features effectively ruined by a global pandemic combined with massive supply shortages meant that grand plans for the future were on hold. It was always going to be a tough year to release a smartphone but, looking back, the Pixel 5 maybe doesn’t get enough credit for making the best of it. more…
fullText:
In 2020, Google Pixel was in a remarkably tough spot. A flailing flagship with one of its central features effectively ruined by a global pandemic combined with massive supply shortages meant that grand plans for the future were on hold. It was always going to be a tough year to release a smartphone but, looking back, the Pixel 5 maybe doesn’t get enough credit for making the best of it.

Our Damien Wilde reviewed the Pixel 5 and called it an “exercise in compromise,” and I think that sums up this device quite nicely, perhaps even better than we thought at the time. 

On the surface level, the Pixel 5 felt like a weird step forward after the Pixel 4 series. A much less powerful chipset wrapped up in a plastic “bio-resin” that replaced metal and glass was completely out of the ordinary for a flagship smartphone. Yet, it also addressed some of the Pixel 4’s failings by going back to a fingerprint sensor, by packing in a much larger battery, and by feeling a bit more familiar to what had come before after the prior year’s big swing on design.

The Pixel 4 is my favorite Google smartphone hardware to date, and it still holds up

And, looking back on it today, this thing aged quite well!

	
	

It’s still odd to think of this as a “flagship” as, across the board, it was a better fit in the mid-range category. Yet, through and through, it managed to nail down the fundamentals of the hardware. It feels good in a way that’s unique. Where the plastic Pixel 4a had virtually the same design, the Pixel 5’s resin material added some extra grip while managing to feel just a bit more premium. I’m not sure I ever appreciated it enough at the time, but with virtually everything going all-in on shatterable glass and heavy metal in 2026, a durable material like this is so refreshing.

Ultimately, Google’s Pixel 5 was a device that didn’t fit in. We’ll probably never know all of the details around its development, but it’s been said that, at some point, Google apparently wanted Tensor to debut in this time frame rather than ultimately launching a year later on the Pixel 6. We found evidence that suggested the switch wasn’t as last-minute as suggested, but even without such a radical change on deck, the Pixel 5 was absolutely born out of a rough series of circumstances and, looking back, it wasn’t half bad.

Did you have a Pixel 5? Do you remember it fondly?

These are Messages features that Google announced or have been spotted in the wild by beta users.

Messages for web removing QR code pairing

Going forward, Messages for web users will have to use Google Account sign-in. As of late April, the QR code method is still available.

Read receipts are now placed in a circle at the bottom-right corner of message bubbles and images. You swipe left to see timestamps and the encryption lock, while you can swipe right to reply. This first started appearing in August of 2024, but is now seeing wide beta and stable availability.

title: Google Messages rolls out new long-press menu with partial copying [Updated]
snippet: After testing got underway in January, Google Messages is finally widely rolling out a new long-press menu in conversations. more…
fullText:
After testing got underway in January, Google Messages is finally widely rolling out a new long-press menu in conversations.

Update 10/1: Google announced yesterday that the “new long-press redesign for Google Messages has officially launched.”

This update introduces a more intuitive way to interact with your conversations, featuring a tap-activated menu that puts your most-used actions front and center.

There’s also “full support” for light and dark themes, while the experience is now “optimized for landscape mode, ensuring the menu remains accessible and easy to navigate on wider screens.”

The company noted how the “ability to copy only a portion of a text message” was “one of the most requested features.” To do so:

	

Long press any message to bring up the new action menu.

Long press again directly on the text within that message.

Drag the selection handles to highlight the exact part of the message you want to select.

A second dialogue box will appear with options to Copy, Translate, or Select All.

Related: Google Messages rolls out new swipe for timestamps & reply gesture

Original 9/24: This new design replaces the top toolbar that housed various actions. Google only surfaced three actions with everything else in an overflow menu.

	

Upon long-pressing on a chat message or image, Google will show a floating menu with Remix (photos), Reply, Forward, Copy (text), Star, Delete, Select more, Info, and Save (photos).

Each action is accompanied by an icon at the front for quick scanning, while Copy lets you highlight a specific part of the message by pressing down and dragging the bubble. Previously, you could only copy the entire message.

If you’ve selected the newest message in a thread, Google will somewhat center it with a bouncy animation and haptic feedback. Messages prominently blurs the background layer when this menu is active. The row of emoji and “Create” Photomoji shortcuts is unchanged.

As of today, we’re seeing the new Google Messages long-press menu widely rolled out with stable version 20260910_03_RC02. There is a server-side component, so be sure to Force stop from the App info menu if it’s not yet live.

snippet: Fall is a big season for sports fans, and ESPN recently launched a big upgrade for users of its tvOS and iOS apps: 4K HDR streaming. more…
fullText:
Fall is a big season for sports fans, and ESPN recently launched a big upgrade for users of its tvOS and iOS apps: 4K HDR streaming.

ESPN streaming service now supports 4K HDR, with tvOS and iOS apps first to add support

In the last few weeks, ESPN began rolling out a big upgrade in its tvOS and iOS apps.

The streaming service now offers 4K HDR quality for top programming, including live games from the NFL, NBA, NHL, and more.

From ESPN’s press release last month:

This week, ESPN and ESPN2 will begin rolling out in 4K HDR in the U.S., elevating picture quality for fans during one of the highest stakes stretches of the year for live sports. This includes all ESPN productions of Monday Night Football, NBA and NHL plus select live events across college football and US Open tennis, and marquee live events like Super Bowl LXI. This update will deliver clearer edges, sharper colors and smoother movement — all critically important for delivering a richer and more immersive viewing experience for sports fans.

The ESPN App on iOS and tvOS will be the first to support the new experiences, with additional connected TV platforms to follow, as well as on Disney+ in the U.S. to ESPN Unlimited subscribers.

When browsing the ESPN app, you’ll see a new ‘4K HDR’ tag for content that supports the higher-quality video stream.

If you have a strong internet connection at home or on the go, 4K HDR will provide a more vibrant, crisp, premium image for your favorite sports content.

For any sports fans tempted to splurge on an Apple TV 4K for the first time, we recommend holding out just a little bit longer. The wait for a new Apple TV model is reportedly almost over.

title: iOS 27 gives Apple Photos two features we’ve waited a long time for
snippet: iOS 27 is packed with new features for Apple’s Photos app, including two that have long been on many users’ wish lists: full-featured slideshow creation and upgraded iCloud Shared Albums. more…
fullText:
iOS 27 is packed with new features for Apple’s Photos app, including two that have long been on many users’ wish lists: full-featured slideshow creation and upgraded iCloud Shared Albums.

#1: Slideshow creation and customization

The Photos app has long supported a very rudimentary version of a slideshow feature. But it’s geared more toward reliving personal memories. If you wanted to create a slideshow for an event or other public viewing, you had to look elsewhere.

But in iOS 27, Photos finally adds a robust set of slideshow creation tools.

You can now play any set of photos or videos as a slideshow, customizing things like transition style, duration, and music. You can auto-loop the slideshow, and even save it as a video file for easy re-viewing.

Robust slideshow features are a long-overdue addition to the Photos app, but I’m thrilled that they’re finally here.

You may not know that the Photos app has its own social network-style feature: Shared Albums.

iCloud Shared Albums let you have an album that’s shared with friends or family. You get an activity feed to show new photos and videos that are added, and you have the option to like or comment on anything shared. It’s a lot like old-school Instagram, but private and limited to people you choose to share with.

I love the feature, and iOS 27 brings some long-awaited upgrades. You can now share full resolution photos and videos (they were lower quality before), react with any emoji, set new participant permissions, and Android and Windows users can now add photos too.

Shared Albums are improving just in time for Apple’s new HomePad device, and these upgrades make me even more excited for that product.

title: M6 Mac release schedule: Here’s when to expect new Macs
snippet: Apple next-generation M6 chip arrived last week in the new Mac mini. But several more products will get M6 upgrades soon. Here’s the rumored release schedule for M6 Macs—plus the M6 iPad Pro. more…
fullText:
Apple next-generation M6 chip arrived last week in the new Mac mini. But several more products will get M6 upgrades soon. Here’s the rumored release schedule for M6 Macs—plus the M6 iPad Pro.

This fall: M6 MacBook Pro, M6 iMac

This fall, likely in October or early November, Apple is rumored to launch two new M6 Macs:

MacBook Pro

iMac

The MacBook Pro will be only the 14-inch base model. Per Mark Gurman, Apple is skipping Pro and Max versions of the M6 chip. As a result, only the entry MacBook Pro will get M6 while the next Pro-level chips coming will be M7 Pro and M7 Max in 2027.

Apple’s new iMac isn’t expected to change much beyond the M6 chip. The only other rumored upgrade is a fresh slate of colors. But the jump from M4 to M6 should make the new model a worthy update nonetheless.

Notably absent from this list is the rumored touchscreen MacBook Pro / Ultra. It’s expected to launch soon too, but will use M5 Pro and M5 Max chips instead of the M6.

Early 2027: M6 MacBook Air, M6 iPad Pro

After this fall, the next products rumored to get M6 upgrades are:

MacBook Air

iPad Pro

A new M6 MacBook Air is expected to launch in early 2027. Anytime in the February-April window is possible, but based on Apple’s history, March is a safe bet.

Other than a chip upgrade, there are minimal rumors about the new MacBook Air. It should retain the same design as the M5 model. And reporting dates an OLED upgrade as coming no sooner than 2028, so the display will likely be unchanged too.

Apple last updated the iPad Pro in fall 2025, when it got the M5 chip. Rumors point to a spring 2027 update coming, meaning the product will follow its typical 18-month upgrade cycle.

Beyond getting the M6 chip, Apple’s new iPad Pro is expected to add a vapor chamber for cooling. That should boost sustained performance in the ultra-thin device.

One potential M6 benefit for both the MacBook Air and iPad Pro is that it could boost battery life. Apple says the M6’s 2-nanometer process brings “a major leap in performance and power efficiency.”

title: Apple TV unveils chilling serial killer thriller based on bestselling novel
snippet: Today Apple TV unveiled the trailer for Nocturne, a new thriller series based on bestselling crime novel “The Sandman” by Lars Kepler. more…
fullText:
Today Apple TV unveiled the trailer for Nocturne, a new thriller series based on bestselling crime novel “The Sandman” by Lars Kepler.

Nocturne is new thriller series premiering October 30

Apple TV has a variety of exciting crime thrillers in its library, and this fall it plans to add even more. 

One of those series—Nocturne—is based on the bestselling novel “The Sandman” by Lars Kepler.

Nocturne premieres Friday, October 30 with two episodes, followed by weekly releases through December 25.

The show revolves around a serial killer and stars Liev Schreiber and Zazie Beetz, with Stephen Graham (“Adolescence”) as the killer.

Apple just released the trailer, offering our first proper preview of the chilling new show. Here’s the official summary for Nocturne, followed by the trailer.

“Nocturne” tells the story of Jonah Lynn (Schreiber), an ex-soldier turned homicide detective who, tired of working the tough streets of Philadelphia, moves to a small town in Western Pennsylvania for a quiet life. But, as the town and his family come under attack from the diabolically cunning serial killer Jurek Walter (Graham), Jonah must protect all that he holds dear. When the desperate search for Jurek’s last missing victim forces Jonah to send his surrogate daughter FBI Agent Saga Bauer (Beetz), up against Jurek, how far will Jonah go?

Two weeks before Nocturne, ‘12 12 12’ premieres on Apple TV as another crime thriller. It stars Anthony Mackie and Jamie Dornan and centers around a heist, covering the 12 months of planning, 12 hours of the heist itself, and 12 days following it.

Looking beyond the fall, Apple plans to kick off 2027 with the high-profile thriller The Wanted Man, which stars Hugh Laurie as an organized crime boss.

title: New MacBook Pro redesign gets exciting launch timing update
snippet: Apple reportedly plans to launch new Home products on October 13. And according to Mark Gurman, it sounds like the rumored MacBook Pro redesign will arrive shortly after. more…
fullText:
Apple reportedly plans to launch new Home products on October 13. And according to Mark Gurman, it sounds like the rumored MacBook Pro redesign will arrive shortly after.

Redesigned MacBook Pro with touchscreen to be introduced in October or November, per Mark Gurman

Today Bloomberg launched a new weekly podcast: ‘Power On with Mark Gurman.’ In the inaugural episode, Gurman provides a launch timing update for Apple’s rumored new MacBook Pro redesign with a touchscreen, OLED, and more.

Here’s what he said:

Apple, I believe, will introduce its first touchscreen MacBook Pro this fall, as early as October. It could slip to November, but as early as October. And Apple is testing it internally using macOS 27.2, which is a beta that they’ve already put out to developers in recent weeks. So this thing is approaching.

Apple often launches new Macs in the late October-early November window. It sounds like that’s exactly what’s being planned for this new MacBook Pro (or MacBook Ultra) device.

We’ve long been expecting and hoping for a fall launch, but Gurman previously cautioned that the product could slip into early 2027. Now that October has arrived, today’s new update is a great indication that the model is on track to launch soon.

And based on Gurman’s other reporting, it sounds like we could see several new Apple products launch within a few weeks of each other. 

A new Apple TV 4K, ‘HomePad’, and HomePod mini are rumored for October 13, with Macs following in late October or early November. And that’s all in addition to the highly anticipated iPhone Duo, which ships October 23.

title: Gemini app adding Google Wallet integration for ‘personalized insights’
snippet: The latest Gemini Connected App is Google Wallet for “information and personalized insights based on your saved info.” more…
fullText:
The latest Gemini Connected App is Google Wallet for “information and personalized insights based on your saved info.”

Once this integration is enabled, you can “get info from passes, such as loyalty cards, event tickets, and boarding passes.” Prompts include:

Find the boarding pass for my flight to Chicago.

Show me my airline loyalty numbers.

Other capabilities include:

Provide insights based on transaction data from financial accounts you’ve linked with services like Plaid

Summarize expense activity and get budgeting tips

Check and summarize available rewards and special offers based on cards and passes in Google Wallet

The Plaid integration dates back to the Google Pay app and is only available for Google Wallet users in the US. This lets you ask prompts like: “How much did I spend on groceries last month?”

	

The Google Wallet Connected App cannot: 

Make transactions using payment methods in your Google Wallet.

Update or delete connected financial accounts.

Once rolled out for your account, @Google Wallet will work in the prompt box. It will also appear in the Connected Apps list for you to enable. 

At the moment, this integration is only available in the US on personal Google Accounts. We’re not seeing this widely rolled out yet.

Important: We’re gradually making this feature available, so it might not be available to you just yet.

title: Gemini fully replaces Google Assistant on Android
snippet: At the start of September, the Google Assistant deprecation on mobile got underway. It now looks to be widely rolling out. more…
fullText:
At the start of September, the Google Assistant deprecation on mobile got underway. It now looks to be widely rolling out.

Google has been moving Assistant users to Gemini over the past few weeks. This deprecation was originally set for 2025 and later extended to 2026. In early August, Google announced the final timeline.

From various user reports today, this migration appears to be fully underway. Google Assistant is gone on all devices/accounts we checked in the US and Europe.

	

Notably, the Gemini app has removed the “Switch to Google Assistant” setting. This shortcut no longer appears at the bottom of the account menu with Google app 17.60 stable and 17.62 beta.

	

As such, you can no longer “use or switch back to Google Assistant on your phone, tablet, or paired devices.” The latter grouping includes Wear OS, headphones, and Android Auto.

There are no changes to Assistant just yet on “Google Nest and Google Home smart speakers, displays, or other Google Assistant-enabled speakers and displays.”

Gemini is now the “voice assistant experience on Android” when you long-press the power button or swipe from the corners.

title: Using an iPad mini to preview the iPhone Duo experience
snippet: Alongside using the iPhone 18 Pro, I’ve also been carrying out a little experiment as we await the launch of the iPhone Duo. To get a sense of what it might be like to use the large screen of the upcoming device, I’ve been using my iPad mini as a substitute phone some of the time. Given that the screen is a similar size and shape, I’m hoping that it gives me something of a preview of the experience … more…
fullText:
Alongside using the iPhone 18 Pro, I’ve also been carrying out a little experiment as we await the launch of the iPhone Duo.

To get a sense of what it might be like to use the large screen of the upcoming device, I’ve been using my iPad mini as a substitute phone some of the time. Given that the screen is a similar size and shape, I’m hoping that it gives me something of a preview of the experience …

I’ll be the first to admit that I really have no business owning an iPad mini. Most of the time it’s only used as an ebook reader for library books borrowed via the Libby app, as you can’t read these on a Kindle here in the UK. (Don’t get me started on that bizarre omission …)

Given the number of ebooks I read, it’s not totally unreasonable to have a second device more or less devoted to this, but I do feel a slight twinge of guilt that such a capable device has such a limited role. I’ve now, however, found at least a temporary additional task for it: getting some sense of the experience we might expect from an iPhone Duo.

As my colleague Ryan Christoffel recently noted, the interior display of the iPhone Duo is a bit smaller than that of the iPad mini, but the difference isn’t, uh, huge.

Due to the much smaller bezels on iPhone Duo, the difference in screen size isn’t as notable as you might expect:

iPhone Duo: 7.6‑inch display

iPad mini: 8.3-inch display

What I did was to install all of the same apps I have on my iPhone with a similar layout in order to mirror the experience as closely as possible. iPhone Wi-Fi hotspot provides the connectivity needed to allow me to use the iPad on a wide variety of occasions when I would otherwise have been using my iPhone.

In one way, the iPad mini delivers a better experience than the Duo as it runs iPadOS rather than iOS, giving a more flexible multitasking experience. However, I’m not a fan of windowing on such a small screen, so I primarily use apps either full screen or split screen, making it very similar to the Duo interface.

To counter the lack of pocketability, I’ve only taken it with me when I have a backpack, but that’s about half the time when I’m out and about.

Of course, the iPad doesn’t support all the Duo features, so it’s only a very rough and ready approximation of the experience, but it has provided a good sense of what it’s like to have access to this sort of size screen in a phone – and I have very much enjoyed it. 

As with many such comparisons, the greatest impact is not when switching to something new, but switching back to the previous product. Whenever I switch from using the iPad mini back to the iPhone 18 Pro, the screen does seem extremely small. This experiment has done absolutely nothing to reduce my technolust for the upcoming device.

title: iOS 27.2 gives Apple Podcasts the big fix I’ve wanted for years
snippet: Apple Podcasts is my podcast app of choice, but I’ve long had major issues with its central Up Next queue feature. I’m happy to report that iOS 27.2 introduces the solution. more…
fullText:
Apple Podcasts is my podcast app of choice, but I’ve long had major issues with its central Up Next queue feature. I’m happy to report that iOS 27.2 introduces the solution.

iOS 27.2 splits Apple Podcasts ‘Up Next’ queue into two sections: New Episodes and Continue Playing

There’s a lot I appreciate about Apple Podcasts. Transcripts and automatically generated chapters are two killer features that make the app my go-to. And I love all the recent video-related upgrades, too.

But for years, Apple Podcasts’ central ‘Up Next’ queue has regularly tempted me to use a different app.

I’ve written before about why Up Next feels broken. To summarize: 

it does a poor job letting you see what podcasts are available

episodes can easily get lost, even when you’re mid-listen

I’m very excited to report, however, that iOS 27.2 brings an overdue fix for Up Next. And it does that by splitting the feature up into two separate sections:

New Episodes

Continue Playing

At the top of the app is New Episodes, which looks and mostly works just like Up Next did. Except as the name implies, it will only ever show you the latest episodes for each show you follow.

Continue Playing is right underneath it as a central hub for all episodes you’ve started, but haven’t yet completed.

	

These two sections jointly address all of my biggest issues with the previous Up Next queue.

It’s easy to see what’s new at a glance, and I never lose track of episodes anymore, since anything I’ve started will be available in Continue Playing. I still have some smaller quibbles, but these changes alone address my main issues with Up Next.

If you haven’t tried Apple Podcasts in a while, iOS 27.2 is a great time to revisit it.

title: Bose launched wired, yes, wired, earbuds with ANC for $99
snippet: The new Bose Noise Cancelling Wired Earbuds connect via USB-C and work with almost any device. more…
fullText:
The new Bose Noise Cancelling Wired Earbuds connect via USB-C and work with almost any device.

Bose wants to get back to basics, it seems – it just launched a new pair of wired earbuds with ANC, citing a rise in wired listening popularity. The earbuds connect to any USB-C device, using an internal, proprietary DSP to ensure they work in just about any USB-C port. With any source input, the earbuds output a fixed 24bit signal.

Bose is well-known for its Quiet Comfort lineup in recent years, but it didn’t start there. Still, the company can be considered one of the main players responsible for quality ANC in wireless headphones. After all, the QC35’s became the go-to travel option for some time.

This release, however, has literal strings attached. It needs USB-C to operate, not a 3.5mm output as most wired enthusiasts prefer at a minimum. That means you wouldn’t be able to use your own DAC/amp setup.

	

Even still, Bose’s Noise Cancelling Wired Earbuds will be a good option for those who need ANC without the battery anxiety. Bose says the earbuds have two microphones on each bud to power active noise cancellation. Quiet Mode blocks most noise out, and Aware Mode acts as a transparency setting. ANC can also be disabled.

The new wired Bose earbuds are available to pre-order starting today for $99 in Black and White Smoke. Bose says the buds will begin shipping on October 15 for those who order from the official website and Best Buy.

title: Google confirms Photos bug that prevents editing and deleting, fix coming ‘ASAP’
snippet: Google Photos is undoubtedly the best way to manage your photo library on Android and beyond, but a recent bug has been stopping users from being able to commit even the most basic of tasks, including sharing, editing, and even delete images from their collection. Luckily, if you’ve found yourself dealing with these issues, Google has confirmed a fix is on the way. more…
fullText:
Google Photos is undoubtedly the best way to manage your photo library on Android and beyond, but a recent bug has been stopping users from being able to commit even the most basic of tasks, including sharing, editing, and even delete images from their collection. Luckily, if you’ve found yourself dealing with these issues, Google has confirmed a fix is on the way.

Various user reports on Reddit last week confirmed that a recent glitch has been preventing users from interacting with images after they’ve been edited. That includes sharing, adding to galleries, deleting, and re-editing photos, all from changes as simple as cropping an image. Luckily, Google confirmed in a statement with Android Authority — which reported on the app issues late last week — that a fix is being worked on, with the team working to roll it out “ASAP.”

The Google Photos team is working on rolling out a fix ASAP! […] For now, users can try these 2 workarounds: 1) Tap “Save as copy” when saving new edits, and 2) Visit photos.google.com to delete or share already-edited photos.

Until these changes are live, the company recommends either saving your image as a copy when creating new edits (to prevent locking up the original, sole copy of an image) or accessing the web version of Photos to share or delete as needed.

While I can’t say I’ve seen this bug on my own Pixel 11 Pro XL, it does appear that most of the affected users — or at least those reporting the issue online — are sporting the last few generations of Google’s Tensor-powered devices. If you’ve found yourself in that group, keep an eye on the Play Store for an update coming soon.

title: Samsung’s open-ear Galaxy Buds On go official with late October release
snippet: Samsung has officially announced its first truly open-ear Galaxy Buds with the Galaxy Buds On set for a debut in late October. more…
fullText:
Samsung has officially announced its first truly open-ear Galaxy Buds with the Galaxy Buds On set for a debut in late October.

Announced on its newsroom in Korea, Samsung’s Galaxy Buds On are a pair of clip-style earbuds. Made popular by a host of other brands, this design clips onto the side of your ear, positioning the driver into your ear but leaving room for ambient sounds to come through.

Samsung says you can interact with Galaxy Buds On via “a light touch” at the back half of the earbuds while they also feature automatic volume adjustments, actively work to reduce noise leakage, and have upgrade call quality too. The whole thing runs on a Snapdragon chip and packs 9.5 hours of battery life. 

Gemini Live is supported, just like on Samsung’s other recent Galaxy Buds, and there are also head gestures to answer or end calls, dismiss alarms, and more. 

	

The charging case is essentially identical to the one used on Galaxy Buds 4.

title: Amazon’s new Fire TV Stick 4K ditches Android & sideloading for $59.99
snippet: Amazon continues its move away from Android on Fire TV, with its latest Fire TV Stick 4K moving over to Vega OS, though with upgrades including support for using your TV’s USB port for power and a massively improved remote. more…
fullText:
Amazon continues its move away from Android on Fire TV, with its latest Fire TV Stick 4K moving over to Vega OS, though with upgrades including support for using your TV’s USB port for power and a massively improved remote.

Available starting today, the new Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K costs $59.99 – $29.99 as a part of Prime Day deals next week. The new streamer, Amazon touts, is around 20-40% faster in most tasks compared to other 4K streaming devices and TVs while also being smaller than prior generations.

One welcome upgrade here is that you can power the new Fire TV Stick 4K using your TV’s USB port, making it a whole lot easier to power the streamer.

Amazon is also debuting a new remote here which has an asymmetric design that’s flat on top and rounded at the bottom. It has a metal home button for easy recognition, a customizable Star button, and IR controls for your other TV hardware such as a soundbar. Amazon is also launching a standalone version of this remote for other Fire TV devices.

	

The big change compared to the last generation, though, is that the latest Fire TV Stick 4K ditches Android in favor of Vega OS. Amazon’s new platform is indeed faster and continues to add more apps in time – Amazon says over 2,000 apps have been added this year – but it also loses support for sideloading, a popular option among many Fire TV users.

As mentioned, the new Fire TV Stick costs $59.99 and is available for purchase starting today in the US.

title: Google aware of Android Auto bug that blocks calls if your foldable phone is closed
snippet: An Android Auto bug is reportedly blocking outgoing calls from closed foldable phones, like the Motorola Razr. Both Google and Motorola are aware of the issue, which might mean a fix for those affected soon. more…
fullText:
An Android Auto bug is reportedly blocking outgoing calls from closed foldable phones, like the Motorola Razr. Both Google and Motorola are aware of the issue, which might mean a fix for those affected soon.

There is no shortage of form factors in the bucket of Android foldable devices. The most iconic might be the Razr from Motorola, if only for the nostalgia associated with it. Just like the original Razr flip phone in the mid-2000s, and every other foldable, the outer display has at least some use cases. Making or taking calls is a big one.

According to a couple of reports on Motorola and Google forums, the Motorola Razr can’t actually make calls while the phone is closed and connected to Android Auto because of a strange bug (via Android Authority). If an outgoing call is attempted, Android Auto throws an error that suggests opening the phone. When open, outgoing calls go through without issue.

Obviously, that negates the benefit of having a foldable device. And storing your foldable phone somewhere in your car while the internal display is exposed might be neglect, at least, in line with Samsung and Motorola’s suggested care.

	

The bug reports only mention calling from a Motorola Razr connected to Android Auto, ranging from the Razr Ultra 2025 and Razr Ultra 2026.

According to those users, there is a fix. The good news – reverting back to Google Assistant from Gemini solves the problem. The bad news – Google Assistant was just fully removed from Android as a whole on September 28.

Both Google and Motorola are aware of the Android Auto bug. Motorola’s thread lists a response from the company less than two weeks ago. It’s possible the bug is still affecting users, and with Gemini taking over for Google Assistant, the issue might only spread to more users and devices until a fix is widely rolled out.

Are you able to make Android Auto calls while your foldable phone is closed? Or is it working now?

title: Huawei’s Mate 90 Pro Max says ‘why not’ and just lets you add an entire camera
snippet: Huawei has just introduced its new Mate 90 Pro Max in China and the big feature is not the cameras built into the device, but rather the giant one you can add on. more…
fullText:
Huawei has just introduced its new Mate 90 Pro Max in China and the big feature is not the cameras built into the device, but rather the giant one you can add on.

The Huawei Mate 90 Pro Max is the company’s latest flagship, packing a 6.9-inch dual-layer OLED display, Huawei’s in-house Kirin 9050 (or Pro) chip, Harmony OS 7.0, 12GB or 16GB of RAM, a 6,800 mAh battery, IP68/69, and a pretty solid camera setup. The main camera is a 50MP shooter with variable aperture, backed up by a 40MP ultrawide and a 200MP telephoto shooter with 4x optical zoom.

There’s also a 13MP front-facing camera with a 3D depth sensor, split into three different camera cutouts.

It’s not the phone itself that’s so attention-grabbing, though.

	

Huawei has a “Z10” camera module add-on that’s basically just an entire camera you can attach to the phone. It packs a 1-inch camera sensor, up to 10x optical zoom, and a huge detachable lens. Huawei explains (translated):

A multi-lens optical system, a 24mm-240mm focal length, 10x continuous optical zoom, and a  maximum aperture of F2.0-F4.5, combined with a 1-inch sensor, delivers superior imaging capabilities. 

The innovative HyperClick mount allows for a seamless connection to your phone with a single click, enabling instant sharing after shooting – making travel photography incredibly convenient. It naturally captures portrait interactions and realistically reproduces distant skylines, making professional imaging capabilities readily available.

Like the built-in cameras, which the module covers up, this add-on camera uses an RYYB sensor, and it’s a 50MP sensor. It can adjust between a 24mm and 240mm focal length.

The cost of the add-on “Z10” camera is 5,999 CNY, around $900 USD. The Huawei Mate 90 Pro Max itself runs 9,499 CNY, around $1,400. Both are available this week in China.

fullText:
Apple TV has a strong current lineup headlined by hits like Slow Horses, Ted Lasso, Dark Matter, and new Matthew McConaughey comedy Brothers. But there’s a lot more coming soon. Here’s everything new Apple TV has premiering in October.

The Last First: Winter K2

When: October 2

What: Movie

Genre: Documentary

In “The Last First: Winter K2,” Amir Bar-Lev tells a complex, harrowing and moving story that unpacks the industry of extreme mountain climbing and its changing culture. Focusing on a 2021 expedition, mountaineers John Snorri Sigurjónsson, an Icelander, and the Pakistani father-son team of Ali and Sajid Sadpara set out to be the first to summit K2 in the winter, when the mountain’s conditions are the cruelest. The men soon find themselves sharing the treacherous ascent with influencer climbers and their film crews, commercial expedition clients and Nims, a Nepalese celebrity mountaineer, and his team of Sherpas. “The Last First: Winter K2” takes us to the icy heights and unpredictable weather of K2 and reveals a surprising and layered story — one of strategy and determination, class and caste, money and power — all under life and death circumstances.

title: Here’s why I upgraded from the Apple Watch Series 10 to Series 12
snippet: I’m someone who doesn’t often upgrade my Apple Watch right when a new one comes out. The Apple Watch Series 10 I owned prior was only purchased this January, despite initially coming out in September 2024. That said, Apple Watch Series 12 was a highly compelling purchase, despite the fact that the two largely share the same design language. Here’s why I took the leap. more…
fullText:
I’m someone who doesn’t often upgrade my Apple Watch right when a new one comes out. The Apple Watch Series 10 I owned prior was only purchased this January, despite initially coming out in September 2024. That said, Apple Watch Series 12 was a highly compelling purchase, despite the fact that the two largely share the same design language. Here’s why I took the leap.

So yes, the Series 10 and Series 12 largely share the same design. In fact, the Series 12 is arguably a regression because the bezels are slightly thicker. This didn’t bother me, because I use a watch face with a black background anyways.

However, the new features of Apple Watch Series 12 really fascinated me. In particular, I was compelled by the much improved heart-rate monitor, as well as the new ‘Readiness’ app. Everything on the Series 12 also feels substantially faster, especially Siri.

Previous Apple Watches never really gave me what I wanted in terms of health tracking. Series 12 provides much more insight. Before, you sort of just had your activity rings and a bunch of scattered data in the Health app. Now, the new Health app tells you absolutely everything you need to know in an incredibly useful manner.

I am still wearing my WHOOP, primarily because I’d like to compare the two over a longer term before I ditch it fully, but as of now, Apple’s Health app holds up – and I’m happy with what the Apple Watch Series 12 offers in terms of health tracking.

	

Also worth noting that the WHOOP is a $239/year subscription that largely doesn’t offer much over Apple Health anymore.

All in all, my purchase of the Apple Watch Series 12 can be summarized by the fact that the Apple Watch made a major push into getting serious as a health wearable. It no longer feels like as much of an afterthought.

title: Blender, the 3D modeling app, is launching for Android next year; iPad app still on pause
snippet: One of the biggest headaches facing Google’s push to make Android more of a desktop platform is the professional sector of apps and programs, but one big name is making the effort, as Blender is working to bring its app to Android. more…
fullText:
One of the biggest headaches facing Google’s push to make Android more of a desktop platform is the professional sector of apps and programs, but one big name is making the effort, as Blender is working to bring its app to Android.

Blender is an industry-recognized suite of tools used for 3D modeling. It’s effectively the go-to option, and for good reason. 

Shown off at the Blender Conference 2026, Blender is making the effort to bring its app to Android. The hour-long video goes over the details of how the app works and the roadmap for releasing the port, which is targeting a release in the first half of 2027. An APK demo is already available. The port appears to be mainly focused on tablets, which is a bigger undertaking than you might think. Blender relies quite heavily on keyboard shortcuts, so bringing a fully functional experience on a touchscreen is a massive change. It appears that a stylus is a big part of the experience.

This comes at an important time, not only as Android tablets continue to advance, but also as Googlebook makes its debut. The Android-based platform opens up a new desktop-class platform for Blender.

	

Notably, iPad support for Blender is still “on hold” for the time being, despite the work for touchscreen support being brought to the Android app.

title: Apple Music 7.0 beta brings Liquid Glass redesign to Android
snippet: Apple Music for Android is getting a big Liquid Glass-inspired redesign with the latest 7.0 beta. more…
fullText:
Apple Music for Android is getting a big Liquid Glass-inspired redesign with the latest 7.0 beta.

With Liquid Glass now a year old on Apple platforms, the new design language is coming to Android. Apple Music now has a floating bottom bar that lets you see what is above, below, and to the sides. The navigation element has a small amount of translucency that allows you to mostly see solid colors underneath.

Old vs. new

Similarly, the mini-player above it gets the same treatment and is no longer docked with the bottom bar. Compared to Liquid Glass on iOS, scrolling does not collapse the bar into a more compact version, with everything remaining in place.

	

Top bars across the app have been updated, with the page title and overflow menu on the same line. The three-dot icons are no longer themed red and have been placed in circular containers. The Library tab sees the biggest update with “Edit Pins” and “Edit Categories” now part of the overflow.

Artist pages get a big update with the background now themed based on the cover image. This closely matches the iOS design with a more prominent play button and info page that’s no longer at the very bottom. Share has also been placed in the top-right corner.

	

The Settings page has also been modernized with better grouping. There are no major changes to Now Playing, which did not see any big updates on iOS.

Finally, Apple Music 7.0 now has an edge-to-edge design for the status and navigation bars.

With the last release, Apple Music for Android switched to a new versioning system that aligns with iOS. Today’s version 7.0 aligns with iOS 27.

Apple Music 7.0 is currently in beta, with testing usually lasting a few weeks. You can sign up from the Play Store listing or this page. In general, these builds are fairly stable.
